response: Yes, dementia and aphasia can be associated with motor neuron disease (MND), although this connection is not always widely recognized. Research has shown that a subset of patients with MND, particularly those with certain types such as frontotemporal dementia and motor neuron disease (FTD-MND), can exhibit cognitive and language impairments, including dementia and aphasia. These symptoms can occur alongside the more typical motor symptoms of MND, such as muscle weakness and wasting. Increased awareness of this association is important for accurate diagnosis and comprehensive management of patients with MND.
